I'm a bit vexed.

On one hand, .22lr while a little difficult to get your mitts on, is still relatively cheap. I paid roughly a nickel per round without bargain hunting. meanwhile, the cheap .223 i can get is easily a quarter a shot. To say nothing of the more expensive packages. So, I feel like if I just wanted to dump a magazine at a target, that .22lr would be far more economical than .223.

Now, you CAN slap a conversion kit on an AR-15 like I've got and shoot .22lr out of the same barrel that spits .223... But, it's less than ideal. you leave the barrel messy with a bunch of lead, you can foul up your gas tube, and most AR barrels I've seen are 1:7 or 1:9 twist. .22lr is more at home with 1:16, and if you go with the more common AR rifling, you're talking about a loss of accuracy. This doesn't seem ideal for dumping truckloads of .22lr through. But, the dedicated, 1:16 .22lr Uppers I've seen are freaking expensive! Heck, most of them are pricy enough that I may as well buy a whole S&W M&P15-22 to slap a slidefire on.

Doesn't seem right to buy a costly barrel to fire cheap bullets through. Doesn't appeal to me to foul a good barrel that's not well suited to the job either.
